name: Palm Springs
tagline: Flat valley miles, two climbs, the Tour in February
best_months: October to April. The Tour de Palm Springs FAQ puts February highs at 60 to 70 and lows at 50 to 55. PJAMM puts June-to-September highs at the foot of Highway 74 at 102 to 108 F and says not to start after sunrise then; Velo Palm Springs gives Joshua Tree a riding window of roughly October to April. The Desert Bicycle Club's weekend rides are on its calendar from October, and Big Wheel Bikes' Palm Springs store closes for the summer.
summary: Palm Springs is a winter riding town at the west end of the Coachella Valley. The flat miles are on CV Link, the car-free path that runs 20 miles from the Palm Springs Visitor Center to Cathedral City. The two climbs are Tramway Road in town and Highway 74 out of Palm Desert. The Tour de Palm Springs, the valley's big charity ride, starts downtown on South Palm Canyon on a Saturday in February; in 2027 that is February 6. The airport is two miles from downtown. Delta and American check a packed bike as a standard bag, $45 each way (Oct 2026). One Palm Desert shop builds a shipped bike, and three valley shops rent carbon road bikes. Bring yours for a week; rent for the Tour alone.
about: Palm Springs sits at the west end of the Coachella Valley, and the riding runs the length of it: Cathedral City, Rancho Mirage, Palm Desert, Indian Wells, La Quinta and Indio down Highway 111, with Desert Hot Springs across Interstate 10. This guide covers all of them. Its zones: Palm Springs itself (downtown, Tramway Road, the Visitor Center where CV Link starts); the valley floor along CV Link and Highway 111; the climbs, Tramway Road in town and Highway 74 south out of Palm Desert; and the car days, Box Canyon at the east end of the valley and Joshua Tree National Park over the hills to the north. Every listing says which one it sits in. The group rides are in Palm Desert, about 12 miles down the valley, so a rider sleeping downtown rides to them or drives.

The Tour de Palm Springs is on this site's 2027 calendar: Saturday, February 6, 2027, routes from 16 to 101 miles from South Palm Canyon downtown, run by CVSPIN and Perimeter Bicycling for Coachella Valley charities. Robert is riding it. Packet pickup is Friday noon to 8 p.m. and Saturday from 6 a.m. at South Palm Canyon and Baristo; the century rolls at 6:30 and the 16-mile route at 9:30 (the Tour's FAQ and registration page, Oct 2026). The organizer says the 2027 routes use CV Link where they can and the maps were still to come when we read the page. The valley's group riding runs through one club, the Desert Bicycle Club in Palm Desert, whose calendar is public and whose rides take guests with no sign-up.
riding: The ride for the day you land is CV Link: the paved, car-free path from the Palm Springs Visitor Center at Highway 111 and Tramway Road, along the Whitewater River to Date Palm Drive in Cathedral City. 20 miles, join anywhere, turn around anywhere. Tramway Road starts at the same corner: 4 miles and 1,900 feet at 9.5 percent, steepening all the way, and bikes stop at the tramway's toll gate about half a mile below the top. The big climb is Highway 74 south out of Palm Desert, 14 miles and 3,700 feet, with little or no shoulder past the first few miles and traffic at highway speed. The easy town loop is Velo Palm Springs' 8-mile Midcentury Modern ride through downtown's landmark houses. Palm Desert and Rancho Mirage, where CV Link has its gap, ride on a 14-mile loop from Tri-A-Bike's door. The car days are Box Canyon from Mecca, Joshua Tree's Park Boulevard, and Geology Tour Road for dirt. In the hot months, roughly May to October, start at dawn or don't start: PJAMM puts June-to-September highs in Palm Desert at 102 to 108 F.

The group rides are in Palm Desert, and they take guests with no sign-up. The Desert Bicycle Club's {ride:palm-desert-ca-desert-bicycle-club-saturday-rides|Saturday rides} leave Palm Desert Civic Park in four groups, two that drop and two that regroup. Its {ride:palm-desert-ca-desert-bicycle-club-sunday-climbers|Sunday Climbers} ride Highway 74 from the Starbucks at El Paseo at your own pace, regrouping at the Art Smith Trailhead and the Vista Point. In winter its {ride:palm-desert-ca-desert-bicycle-club-palm-springs-ride|Monday ride to Palm Springs} leaves Bike N Brews on Highway 111 and turns at Koffi in Rancho Mirage. {ride:palm-desert-ca-tri-a-bike-saturday-fun-ride|Tri-A-Bike's fun ride} from the shop on San Pablo is the slow one, any bike. In Palm Springs itself, {ride:palm-springs-ca-big-wheel-bikes-community-group-rides|Big Wheel Bikes' community rides} run November to April and go up on the shop's Instagram and Facebook, not on a fixed day, so follow the shop before you come. The club's easier C rides, 20 to 35 miles at about 13 to 14 mph, start from a different place each week and are posted on its C Rides Facebook page. The rides hub for the valley is /rides/ca/palm-desert/.
getting_there: Fly into Palm Springs International (PSP), about two miles east of downtown; Tahquitz Canyon Way runs from the terminal to Palm Canyon Drive. Alaska, Southwest, United, Delta, American, WestJet, Air Canada and Sun Country fly it, much of it winter-only (a flight-search page, Oct 2026). Rental car counters are in the terminal's north wing; SunLine buses carry a built bike on a front rack but not a case. Driving, downtown Los Angeles is about 100 miles west and downtown Phoenix about 260 miles east in a straight line; the road is longer. You don't need a car for the Tour or the valley floor: the start, packet pickup, a repair shop and a rental fleet are all in Palm Springs, and the Palm Desert shops deliver a rental to a hotel. Highway 74, Joshua Tree and Box Canyon are car days. The Bring-your-bike page has the airline rules, the shop that builds a shipped bike and SunLine's bike rules.

routes.name: CV Link, West Valley (Palm Springs to Cathedral City)
routes.surface: Wide paved path, with a decomposed-granite walking and running path beside it on most of it. The Palm Desert piece switches between path and street.

start.name: Palm Springs Visitor Center, Highway 111 at Tramway Road (the west end)

routes.description: Zone 2, the valley floor, and the ride for the day you land. The valley's car-free path: about 40 miles in three pieces, finished in 2025. The Palm Springs piece runs 19.63 miles from the Palm Springs Visitor Center, along the Chino Wash and the Whitewater River levee, to Date Palm Drive in Cathedral City. A spur follows Tahquitz Creek through Demuth Park. Join it anywhere and turn around anywhere; there's an access point with street parking at Via Escuela and Executive Drive, just east of Gene Autry Trail. CVAG posts no hours, and solar lights set in the path mark it at night. The other two pieces are in Palm Desert (5.44 miles, Bump and Grind trailhead to Cook Street) and from La Quinta to Coachella (16.02 miles, Washington Street to Airport Boulevard). The west end is the foot of Tramway Road, so the two make one day: flat miles out, the wall on the way back.
routes.water: Hydration stations at the rest stops. Patch counted 30 rest stops with benches, bike racks and hydration stations (Sept 2026). CVAG lists restrooms at the Palm Springs Visitor Center, Esperanza Park, the Bump and Grind access point, Palm Desert Civic Park, North Jackson Park and Sierra Vista Park.
routes.hazards: You share it with e-bikes, electric scooters and golf carts. The limit is 20 mph for bikes and carts and 15 for scooters (CVAG). It isn't one path end to end. Rancho Mirage and Indian Wells pulled out of the project, so the path stops at their city lines (Palm Springs Post, Nov 2025): the West Valley piece ends at Date Palm Drive, and the next piece starts in Palm Desert. In November 2025 Palm Springs listed work under way at the Sunrise Way undercrossing and along the Tahquitz Creek corridor. Check the CVAG map before a long ride. Wind can come up at any time. Heat: in the hot months, roughly May to October, ride early or late (Coachella Valley Independent, April 2026); PJAMM puts June-to-September highs in Palm Desert at 102 to 108 F.

routes.name: Tramway Road
routes.surface: Paved road; a separated paved path runs beside it on the south side.

start.name: Tramway Road at Highway 111 (the Palm Springs Visitor Center, the west end of CV Link)

routes.description: Zone 1, the climb you can ride to from a downtown hotel. Tramway Road from Highway 111 up toward the Palm Springs Aerial Tramway's valley station: 3.8 miles and 1,918 feet at 9.5 percent average (PJAMM), steepening all the way; myCols puts the max at 13.9 percent and Palm Springs Life says the last quarter mile touches 19. The 2013 Tour of California finished Stage 2 here. It starts where CV Link starts, so it pairs with the path: flat miles out, the wall on the way back. RideWithGPS 11063650 is an 18.5-mile loop from downtown that climbs it. The tram car itself is under Off the bike.
routes.water: CVAG lists restrooms at the Palm Springs Visitor Center at the foot (see the CV Link entry). Nothing on the climb is named on any page fetched.
routes.hazards: Bikes stop at the tramway's toll gate, about half a mile below the parking lot (Palm Springs Life, 2024; riders on PJAMM and myCols say the same, since about 2014), so the posted 3.8 miles is to a line you can't ride to. The top is 19 percent. Heat: in the hot months, roughly May to October, ride early or late (Coachella Valley Independent, April 2026); PJAMM puts June-to-September highs in the valley at 102 to 108 F, so this one is dawn or not at all.

routes.name: Highway 74, Palms to Pines (from Palm Desert)
routes.surface: Paved two-lane state highway, in good condition, with little or no shoulder after the first few miles.

start.name: Starbucks at Highway 74 and El Paseo, Palm Desert (the foot of the climb)

routes.description: Zone 3, the valley's big climb. Highway 74 south out of Palm Desert, 13.9 miles and 3,677 feet at 5.1 percent average, with the steepest quarter mile at 8.3 percent (PJAMM). The road leaves the desert floor, enters the national forest around mile 3.6, and stacks hairpins from mile 4.5 to 8; the Coachella Valley Vista Point at mile 8.4 looks down on all of them. The grade eases near 4,000 feet at the PJAMM finish. Turn there, or keep going toward Pinyon and Idyllwild (Bikemap's 27-mile route to the top of the pass climbs about 4,800 feet). {ride:palm-desert-ca-desert-bicycle-club-sunday-climbers|The Desert Bicycle Club's Sunday Climbers} ride it from the Starbucks at your own pace, regrouping at the Art Smith Trailhead (mile 4) and the Vista Point. From downtown Palm Springs the foot of the climb is about 12 miles down the valley.
routes.hazards: No to minimal shoulder, and traffic at highway speed both ways; PJAMM calls it 'not a ride for the traffic averse cyclist', and one rider there (April 2023) turned around for it. The club's own warning: past mile 4 the road is narrow and winding with no bike lane. Riders descend at 35 to 40 mph with cars passing at 65. No water, store or restroom on the climb is named on any page fetched; the Vista Point is a 16-car lot. Heat: June-to-September highs run 102 to 108 F, and PJAMM says don't start after sunrise then; in the hot months, roughly May to October, this is a dawn ride.

routes.name: Tour de Palm Springs century
routes.surface: Paved road and path. The organizer says the 2027 routes use CV Link where they can.

start.name: South Palm Canyon Dr at Tahquitz, downtown Palm Springs

routes.description: Zones 1 and 2, the long one, and Robert's ride. The long route of the Tour de Palm Springs, the valley's big charity ride. It starts and finishes downtown on South Palm Canyon at Tahquitz. The 2027 ride is Saturday, February 6, with routes from 16 to 101 miles; the organizer says the full 2027 maps are coming. A RideWithGPS route of it is 101.4 miles and 3,161 feet; Velo Palm Springs' write-up of an earlier century runs out to Thermal and back. The century rolls at 6:30 a.m.; packet pickup is Friday noon to 8 and Saturday from 6 at South Palm Canyon and Baristo (the Tour's FAQ, Oct 2026). Koffi Palm Springs Central on Tahquitz Canyon Way opens at 6:30 (see Coffee).
routes.water: On event day, 3 lunch stops, 2 snack stops and 4 water stops along the routes (organizer). Nothing published for riding it on another day.
routes.hazards: The organizer says routes and departures can be changed by the host cities, and the 2027 maps weren't out on Oct 3, 2026, so the RideWithGPS line may not be this year's course. On any other day these are open roads with no support; Highway 111, the valley's spine, is its fast road (see Bring your bike). You need the helmet sticker to get into a SAG stop (the Tour's FAQ). Heat: February highs run 60 to 70 (the Tour's FAQ); in the hot months, roughly May to October, PJAMM puts June-to-September highs in Palm Desert at 102 to 108 F, so riding this course out of season is a dawn start.

routes.name: The Midcentury Modern loop (downtown Palm Springs)

start.name: Palm Springs Art Museum Architecture and Design Center
start.address: 300 S Palm Canyon Dr, Palm Springs, CA

routes.description: Zone 1, the downtown easy ride. Velo Palm Springs' loop: 7.86 miles, mostly flat with one short climb. It passes eight landmark buildings, among them the Del Marcos Hotel, Albert Frey's Fire Station No. 1 and Frey House II, Sinatra's Twin Palms and the Kaufmann Desert House. The route uses Palm Canyon Drive, Baristo Road, Indian Canyon Drive, Palisades Drive, Alejo Road, Ladera Circle, Hermosa Place and Vista Chino. Do it the evening you land or on a slow morning. It starts at the Architecture and Design Center (see Off the bike), a block south of the Tour start. Street parking on Palm Canyon is metered, and the Civic Center has a parking structure.
routes.hazards: Palm Canyon Drive carries traffic. Velo Palm Springs says to ride it early, when it's cooler and there's less traffic on Palm Canyon. Heat: in the hot months, roughly May to October, ride early or late (Coachella Valley Independent, April 2026); PJAMM puts June-to-September highs in the valley at 102 to 108 F.

routes.name: Gerald Ford, Tamarisk and Country Club loop (Palm Desert and Rancho Mirage)
routes.surface: Bike lanes and residential streets, with a stretch on the Abrams-Butler trail.

start.name: Tri-A-Bike, Palm Desert
start.address: 44841 San Pablo Ave, Palm Desert, CA 92260

routes.description: Zone 2, the way to ride Palm Desert and Rancho Mirage, where CV Link has its gap. A loop of 14-plus miles from Tri-A-Bike's door, from the shop's own list of local rides. It takes San Pablo, Magnesia Falls, Portola, Gerald Ford, Tamarisk, Frank Sinatra, the Abrams-Butler trail and Country Club, among others. Rancho Mirage isn't on CV Link, so this is how you cross it. The shop calls it easy, with a moderate uphill on Portola and on Gerald Ford to Monterey, and lists Trojan Plaza as a second start. {ride:palm-desert-ca-tri-a-bike-saturday-fun-ride|The shop's weekly fun ride} leaves from the same door, any bike.
routes.hazards: The shop's page names only the uphill on Portola and Gerald Ford, and says nothing about traffic on the rest. Heat: in the hot months, roughly May to October, ride early or late (Coachella Valley Independent, April 2026); PJAMM puts June-to-September highs in Palm Desert at 102 to 108 F.

routes.name: Box Canyon from Mecca

start.name: 66 Ave and Johnson Rd, near Mecca

routes.description: Zone 4, a car day at the east end of the valley. Tri-A-Bike's ride from 66 Ave and Johnson Rd through Box Canyon to Pinto Road at Interstate 10. That's 19.5 miles one way with a shuttle back, or 39 miles if you turn around and ride down. The shop puts the climbing at 1,590 feet.
routes.hazards: The shop rates it advanced. It climbs all the way to the turnaround or the shuttle pickup at I-10. The page names no water stop on the route, so carry all you need, and nothing on the page says what the shoulder or the traffic is like. Heat: this is the low, open end of the valley; in the hot months, roughly May to October, ride early or late (Coachella Valley Independent, April 2026); PJAMM puts June-to-September highs in Palm Desert at 102 to 108 F.

routes.name: Park Boulevard, Joshua Tree National Park
routes.surface: Paved park road, mostly without a shoulder.

start.name: West Entrance, Joshua Tree National Park

routes.description: Zone 4, a car day over the hills to the north. The main road through the Mojave side of the park. It runs roughly 25 miles between the West and North entrances, over moderate rolling hills (Velo Palm Springs, April 2026). Keys View Road, a paved spur, is a climb of roughly five miles from its turnoff on Park Boulevard to the overlook. A rider pays $15 for a seven-day pass (Velo Palm Springs, read Oct 3, 2026). Velo puts the riding window at roughly October to April.
routes.water: None on the park's interior roads. Water only at the park entrances and at the Cottonwood, Black Rock and Indian Cove campgrounds (Velo Palm Springs).
routes.hazards: There are no bike lanes anywhere in the park, and most paved roads have no shoulder. There is no shade. Cell service is unreliable. Heat: summer temperatures regularly pass 100 F and have reached 124 F (Velo Palm Springs), which is why the riding window is October to April. Keys View Road is exposed and the wind can be strong there; descend carefully.

routes.name: Geology Tour Road, Joshua Tree National Park
routes.surface: Dirt road. Riders on wider tires handle it well, per Velo Palm Springs; drivers are told to bring a high-clearance vehicle for the lower section.

start.name: Geology Tour Road at Park Boulevard

routes.description: Zone 4, the dirt ride, on the same car day as Park Boulevard. An 18-mile out-and-back on dirt (not a loop). It drops south from Park Boulevard through some of the park's most interesting geology, per Velo Palm Springs. Bikes are allowed on every paved and dirt road in the park that's open to cars. No valley shop was found renting a gravel bike; the full-suspension rentals in Palm Desert and Palm Springs would do.
routes.water: None. Velo Palm Springs says to carry extra water here.
routes.hazards: It's remote and shadeless, and there's nothing out there if something goes wrong (Velo Palm Springs). Cell service in the park is unreliable. Heat: summer temperatures in the park regularly pass 100 F and have reached 124 F (Velo Palm Springs); ride it in the October-to-April window, early.

coffee.name: Starbucks, Highway 74 and El Paseo
coffee.note: Zone 3, Palm Desert, where Highway 74 meets El Paseo, and the start of {ride:palm-desert-ca-desert-bicycle-club-sunday-climbers|the Desert Bicycle Club's Sunday Climbers}: up Highway 74 at your own pace and back down, regrouping at the Art Smith Trailhead (mile 4) and the Vista Point, per the club. A chain store with a patio; it's here because the climb leaves from it. Two listings give different hours and neither is the store's own, so check; both have it open before the ride.

coffee.name: The Coffee Bean & Tea Leaf, El Paseo
coffee.address: 73400 El Paseo Dr, Palm Desert, CA 92260
coffee.note: Zone 2, Palm Desert, at El Paseo and San Pablo: the valley's weekday ride-out. The Desert Bicycle Club's weekday A and B rides leave from here in winter (club calendar, Oct 2026; they aren't in the directory yet, so check the club's calendar for the day and time), and the store is open before they roll: 5:30 a.m. on weekdays, 6 on weekends, per the chain's store page. A chain. Nothing on bike parking.
coffee.hours_hint: 5:30 a.m. to 7 p.m. Monday to Friday; 6 a.m. to 7 p.m. Saturday and Sunday

coffee.name: Koffi Rancho Mirage 111 Café
coffee.note: Zone 2, Rancho Mirage, the coffee at the turnaround of {ride:palm-desert-ca-desert-bicycle-club-palm-springs-ride|the Desert Bicycle Club's winter ride to Palm Springs}: the club's own page names Koffi in Rancho Mirage as the destination. Koffi is the valley's own roaster, and the roastery is here, on Highway 111 three blocks west of The River. Open 6:30 to 5:30 every day. Nothing on its page about bike parking.

coffee.name: Koffi Palm Springs Central
coffee.address: 650 E Tahquitz Canyon Way, Palm Springs, CA 92262
coffee.note: Zone 1, downtown: the early coffee on the morning of the Tour de Palm Springs. Open at 6:30 every day, on Tahquitz Canyon Way, the cross street of the Tour's start on South Palm Canyon; the century rolls at 6:30. Koffi has five cafés in the valley and this one is the bakery for all of them, in Kaptur Plaza near the Convention Center, with an outdoor patio facing the San Jacintos. Koffi South (1700 S Camino Real, next to the Ace Hotel) keeps the same hours for the south end of town. Nothing on its page about bike parking.

coffee.name: Townie Bagels
coffee.address: 650 E Sunny Dunes Rd, Palm Springs, CA 92264
coffee.note: Zone 1, the Sunny Dunes neighborhood east of downtown: breakfast after the ride in Palm Springs. Water-boiled bagels, breakfast sandwiches and cold brew. Open 6:30 a.m. to noon, closed Tuesday (its own page), so it's early enough for a ride-out and gone by lunch. Taqueria Tlaquepaque's second store is in the same plaza. Nothing on its page about bike parking.

coffee.name: Main Street Coffee, Old Town La Quinta
coffee.address: 78100 Main St, Suite 102, La Quinta, CA 92253
coffee.note: Zone 2, the east-valley stop: Tri-A-Bike's 20-mile ride from the shop ends at the coffee in Old Town La Quinta, about 0.6 mile from the north end of the Bear Creek Trail (the shop's rides page). The shop names Old Town Coffee at this address; the center's own page now lists Main Street Coffee there, open 7 a.m. to 2 p.m. daily. Nothing on bike parking.

restaurants.name: Sherman's Deli & Bakery
restaurants.address: 401 E Tahquitz Canyon Way, Palm Springs, CA 92262
restaurants.note: After the ride, Zone 1: a New York deli on Tahquitz Canyon Way, two blocks east of the Tour start, pastrami and a bakery counter, big portions. Open 8 a.m. to 9 p.m. every day (its own page), so breakfast is there when you get back. There's a second Sherman's at 73161 Country Club Dr in Palm Desert, same hours. Outdoor seating and bike parking weren't on the page.

restaurants.name: King's Highway
restaurants.address: 701 E Palm Canyon Dr, Palm Springs, CA 92264
restaurants.note: The early breakfast, Zone 1: the diner at the Ace Hotel on the south end of town, from 7 a.m. daily. Dinner 4 to 9 Monday to Thursday and 4 to 10 Friday to Sunday (its own page). Indoor and patio tables. Koffi South is next door. The early breakfast in Palm Springs that isn't a bagel.

restaurants.name: Townie Bagels
restaurants.address: 650 E Sunny Dunes Rd, Palm Springs, CA 92264
restaurants.note: Breakfast after the ride, Zone 1, in Sunny Dunes east of downtown: water-boiled bagels and breakfast sandwiches, 6:30 a.m. to noon, closed Tuesday (its own page). Gone by lunch. Also under Coffee.

restaurants.name: Las Casuelas Terraza
restaurants.address: 222 S Palm Canyon Dr, Palm Springs, CA 92262
restaurants.note: The night before the Tour de Palm Springs, Zone 1, on the street it starts on: enchiladas, mole and tamales on three patios, one with a bar and a bandstand, one on the sidewalk. Open 11 a.m. to 10 p.m. Thursday to Monday (its own page), closed Tuesday and Wednesday, so a Friday night works. Reservations online or at (760) 325-2794; large parties by email through the site. A Tour sponsor.

restaurants.name: Lulu California Bistro
restaurants.address: 200 S Palm Canyon Dr, Palm Springs, CA 92262
restaurants.note: The big room for a group the night before, Zone 1: a long menu, an outdoor terrace on Palm Canyon a block from the Tour start, and a mezzanine the site says is for parties. Open 11 to 9 Monday to Thursday, 11 to 10 Friday, 9 a.m. to 10 Saturday, 9 to 9 Sunday (its own page), so it's a Sunday brunch after a ride too. Reservations on OpenTable; (760) 327-5858. A Tour sponsor.

restaurants.name: Taqueria Tlaquepaque
restaurants.address: 362 S Palm Canyon Dr, Palm Springs, CA 92262
restaurants.note: The cheap plate, Zone 1: a carne asada burrito on South Palm Canyon, the Tour's street, with a patio. Its Tripadvisor listing (reviews to Sept 2026) has it open daily to 9, to 10 Friday and Saturday; confirm by phone. A second store sits at 650 E Sunny Dunes Rd, Ste 5, in the same plaza as Townie Bagels, open 8 to 9 daily per its listing. (760) 325-1125.

restaurants.name: Amigo Room at the Ace Hotel
restaurants.address: 701 E Palm Canyon Dr, Palm Springs, CA 92264
restaurants.note: Late, when the day ran long, Zone 1: the Ace's bar is open 4 p.m. to 11 Sunday to Thursday and 4 to 1 a.m. Friday and Saturday, and the kitchen closes an hour before the bar (the hotel's page), so food to 10 most nights and to midnight on the weekend. What the kitchen serves wasn't on the page. A bar, so expect 21 and over.

hotels.name: Hilton Palm Springs
hotels.address: 400 East Tahquitz Canyon Way, Palm Springs, CA 92262
hotels.note: Zone 1, downtown, on Tahquitz Canyon Way four blocks east of Palm Canyon; the Tour de Palm Springs lists it under a mile from the start and names it a lodging sponsor. A full-size hotel: outdoor pool, restaurant, poolside bar, meeting rooms, by its own page. Sherman's Deli is at 401 E Tahquitz, the other side of the street. Self-parking $30 a day; check-in 4, out noon; pets $75 (Oct 2026). Nothing about bikes on the page.

hotels.name: Hyatt Palm Springs
hotels.address: 285 North Palm Canyon Drive, Palm Springs, CA 92262
hotels.note: Zone 1, on Palm Canyon Drive itself, three blocks north of Tahquitz and under a mile from the Tour start by the organizer's list. All suites: 197 of them, each with a separate parlor and a refrigerator, by its page, so there's floor for a bike case. Outdoor pool. Daily resort fee $20 plus tax (Oct 2026). Nothing about bikes on the page.

hotels.name: Hotel Zoso
hotels.address: 150 S Indian Canyon Dr, Palm Springs, CA 92262
hotels.note: Zone 1, a block east of Palm Canyon on Indian Canyon, a block and a half south of Tahquitz; under a mile from the Tour start by the organizer's list. Its own page sells it as a pool-party hotel downtown ("party the weekend away"), with a spa and an airport shuttle folded into a resort fee it doesn't price. The closest bed to the start; a rider who wants quiet the night before picks something else. Nothing about bikes on the page.

hotels.name: Caliente Tropics
hotels.address: 411 E Palm Canyon Dr, Palm Springs, CA 92264
hotels.note: Zone 1, on E Palm Canyon (Highway 111) where it bends east, under two miles from the Tour start by the organizer's list. A 1964 tiki-styled motor hotel, updated, with a pool and parking at the door; its own page calls it "your top choice for Palm Springs hotel rooms at affordable prices." The cheap pick on the Tour's list by its own words, but no rate loaded (Oct 2026). Nothing about bikes on the page.

hotels.name: Ace Hotel & Swim Club
hotels.address: 701 E Palm Canyon Dr, Palm Springs, CA 92264
hotels.note: Zone 1, on E Palm Canyon south of downtown, under three miles from the Tour start by the organizer's list. A converted motel with two pools, a diner (King's Highway) and a bar (the Amigo Room). House bikes: "We've got bikes. They're free, first come, first served," per its survival guide; the FAQ folds bike rentals into the $45-a-night resort fee. Parking $10 a day; check-in after 4, out 11; pets $100 a stay, under 25 lbs (Oct 2026). The main pool is 18 and over. Nothing about bringing your own bike.

hotels.name: Parker Palm Springs
hotels.address: 4200 E. Palm Canyon Drive, Palm Springs, CA 92264
hotels.note: Zone 1, the east end of town: the splurge, 144 rooms on 13 acres at the Cathedral City end of E Palm Canyon, past the Tour's three-mile band (not measured). Its own cycling page lends "complimentary bikes" (beach cruisers with helmets and locks) and hands out the city's cycling map at the concierge desk. Not on the Tour's hotel list. No rate loaded (Oct 2026). Nothing about bringing your own bike.

bike_shops.name: Tri-A-Bike
bike_shops.address: 44841 San Pablo Ave, Palm Desert, CA 92260
bike_shops.note: Zone 2, Palm Desert, about 12 miles southeast of downtown Palm Springs; open since 1987, and one of the two rental shops the Tour de Palm Springs FAQ names. The valley's ship-to-shop shop: it accepts shipped bikes, recommends bikeflights.com, and unboxes and assembles for $150; boxing a bike to ship home is $100 to $150 (Oct 2026). Rents Cannondale or Giant road bikes: aluminum with 105 $75 a day, $200 a week; full carbon with Ultegra $100 a day, $300 a week; carbon with Di2 $124 a day, $350 a week; full-suspension mountain bikes $80 a day, $250 a week (Oct 2026). Helmet, lock and a seat-bag kit; delivery $50 one way to Palm Springs, La Quinta or Indio, $35 to Cathedral City or Rancho Mirage, $25 in Palm Desert; two-day minimum on Tour weekend. Repairs by appointment: check and adjust $95, standard tune-up $150, overhaul $225, a tube swap $20 labor and "within 24 hours during our busy times," 30-day guarantee (Oct 2026). Tuesday to Saturday 10 to 4, closed Sunday and Monday; the site says winter hours resume Oct 19 but does not post them. {ride:palm-desert-ca-tri-a-bike-saturday-fun-ride|Its weekly fun ride} leaves the door, any bike.

bike_shops.name: Big Wheel Bikes CV, Palm Springs
bike_shops.address: 1590 South Palm Canyon Drive, Palm Springs, CA 92264
bike_shops.note: Zone 1, on South Palm Canyon about 2 miles south of the Tour de Palm Springs start: the only rental fleet in Palm Springs. The carbon road rental is a KHS Flite 720: $105 a day, $250 for four days, $350 a week; KHS Flite Team road bikes and full-suspension KHS mountain bikes are $80 a day, $195 for four days, $295 a week (Oct 2026). Helmet, lock and repair kit included; $50 delivery to a resort; two-day minimum on Tour weekend; changes inside 24 hours cost 25 percent. The store was closed for summer until Aug 31 and its winter hours are not posted, so call. The site does not mention repairs. {ride:palm-springs-ca-big-wheel-bikes-community-group-rides|Big Wheel's community group rides} run November to April and are posted on the shop's social accounts. A second store at 74200 Highway 111 in Palm Desert rents Ritte road bikes, (760) 779-1837 ext. 2.

bike_shops.name: Trek Bicycle Palm Springs
bike_shops.address: 611 S Palm Canyon Dr, Suite 24, Palm Springs, CA 92264
bike_shops.note: Zone 1, downtown, on South Palm Canyon under a mile south of Tahquitz Canyon Way, between the Tour start and Big Wheel's rentals. The repair shop in Palm Springs: service on any brand, with "24-hour service turnaround on most service jobs," a free bike check, and pick-up and drop-off for repairs. Level One service $99.99, Level Two $189.99, Level Three from $449.99; boxes a bike to ship home for $79.99 (Oct 2026). Monday to Saturday 9 to 5, closed Sunday. The page lists group rides and clinics but no schedule, and says nothing about rentals, fitting or receiving a shipped bike. The first call for the bike that came out of the case wrong.

bike_shops.name: Palm Desert Bike N Brews
bike_shops.note: Zone 2, Palm Desert, on Highway 111 about 12 miles southeast of downtown Palm Springs, and the winter start of {ride:palm-desert-ca-desert-bicycle-club-palm-springs-ride|the Desert Bicycle Club's Monday ride to Palm Springs}. Road rentals: carbon $140 a day, $300 for three days, $400 a week; aluminum $100, $190 and $300; carbon full-suspension mountain bikes $125 a day (Oct 2026). No makes, models or sizes listed, so call with your height. Helmet and lock included; reserve ahead, walk-ins taken; pickup and drop-off in Palm Springs is $100 for up to five bikes. Repairs: basic tune-up $150, major $200, deluxe $399 (e-bikes more); tube install $10, wheel true $15 to $25, brake bleed $30; fork service $150 to $225, shock $150 to $200; boxes a bike for shipping for $100 to $150 but does not say it receives one (Oct 2026). Turnaround not posted. Tuesday to Saturday 9 to 5, closed Sunday and Monday. The shop's own line is "sales, rentals, e-bikes, shuttles, coffee, beer, components."

bike_shops.name: Trek Bicycle Palm Desert
bike_shops.address: 77750 Country Club Dr, Palm Desert, CA 92211
bike_shops.note: Zone 2, Palm Desert, on Country Club Drive about 12 miles southeast of downtown Palm Springs and north of Highway 111. Service on any brand with 24-hour turnaround: Level One $99.99, Level Two $189.99, Level Three from $449.99, a "Traveling" package at $79.99, and boxing a bike to ship for $79.99 (Oct 2026). Open Monday noon to 5, when Tri-A-Bike and Bike N Brews are closed; Tuesday to Saturday 10 to 6; closed Sunday. Group rides and clinics listed, no schedule. Nothing on rentals, fitting or receiving a shipped bike.

bike_shops.name: Village Peddler
bike_shops.note: Zone 2, La Quinta, in the La Quinta Village across from City Hall, about 17 miles southeast of downtown Palm Springs. Tune-ups, flat repair, wheel truing and adjustments, by appointment only. Open 9 to 4, closed Sunday and Wednesday; summer hours vary. Its rentals are hybrids and cruisers ($40 a day, Oct 2026), not road bikes. The repair page lists "bike shipping" with no detail; ask before you count on it. The repair stop for a rider staying at the east end of the valley.

bike_shops.name: ACME Bike Company
bike_shops.note: Every zone: mobile repair, no storefront. Comes to homes, vacation rentals, RV parks and workplaces in Palm Springs, Rancho Mirage, Palm Desert, Indian Wells, La Quinta and Indio, and says it never charges a service-call fee. Tune-ups, flats, e-bike repair and major repairs; book online or by phone. Prices and hours are not on the home page. For the bike that came out of the box wrong on a Sunday, when every shop in the valley is closed.

culture.name: Palm Springs Aerial Tramway
culture.note: Zone 1, the top of Tramway Road. The rotating tram car from the Valley Station to the Mountain Station at 8,516 feet, about ten minutes up, by the visitor bureau's guide: the rider who climbed Tramway Road wants to see the top, and the one who didn't gets 8,500 feet and snow in February. Adults $36.95 (its tickets page, Oct 2026, with the $2 online fee); winter hours Oct 5, 2026 to May 27, 2027 are first car up 10 a.m. weekdays and 8 a.m. weekends, last car up 8 p.m., last down 9:30 p.m. Parking $15 a car, and it closes about a month each year for maintenance, usually September (visitpalmsprings.com, Sept 2026). Bikes stop at the toll gate below the station (see Routes).

culture.name: Palm Springs Swim Center
culture.address: 405 S Pavilion Way, Palm Springs, CA 92262
culture.note: Zone 1, Sunrise Park, east of downtown off Sunrise Way: the city's outdoor pool, the swim after the ride. Drop-in swimming Monday to Thursday 6 a.m. to 7 p.m., Friday to Sunday 6 a.m. to 3 p.m., closed Tuesdays 8 to 10 a.m. for maintenance; $10 a swim for a non-resident adult, $6 for residents (city page, Oct 2026). The pool's length isn't on the page; (760) 323-8278.

culture.name: Palm Springs Art Museum, Architecture and Design Center
culture.address: 300 S Palm Canyon Drive, Palm Springs, CA 92262
culture.note: Zone 1, on S Palm Canyon a block south of the Tour de Palm Springs start block, in E. Stewart Williams's 1961 glass-and-steel Santa Fe Federal Savings building, and the start of the Midcentury Modern loop (see Routes): architecture and design shows, two hours, the cheap way into the mid-century side of town. Open Thursday noon to 8, Friday to Sunday 10 to 5, closed Monday to Wednesday; $25, free Thursdays 5 to 8 p.m. (Oct 2026). The main museum (101 Museum Drive, two blocks west of Palm Canyon) keeps the same hours, price and free Thursday evening, per its own page.

culture.name: VillageFest
culture.address: 100 S Palm Canyon Drive, Palm Springs, CA 92262
culture.note: Zone 1, downtown: the Thursday night street fair on Palm Canyon Drive, 180-plus vendors, arts, crafts, food, live entertainment, dog-friendly, shops open late, by its own page. Every Thursday, 6 to 10 p.m. October through May and 7 to 10 p.m. June through September (its venue page, Oct 2026). Palm Canyon closes to cars for it. Thursday, February 4, 2027 is the one before the Tour, on the street the Tour starts on two days later.

culture.name: Palm Springs Vinyl Records & Collectibles
culture.address: 220 N Palm Canyon Dr, Palm Springs, CA 92262
culture.note: Zone 1, downtown, on Palm Canyon Dr between Amadeo Rd and Tahquitz Canyon Way, a block north of the Tour start block. Records, CDs, cassettes, posters and music and movie collectibles; it buys as well as sells, and says it has been at it for over 40 years. Open 11 to 6, seven days a week, per its own site (read Oct 3, 2026).

culture.name: The Best Bookstore in Palm Springs
culture.note: Zone 1, downtown, in La Plaza off S Palm Canyon. Independent; its own site calls it a "family-owned bookstore with branches in Palm Springs and San Francisco." Publishers Weekly's piece on its opening names an LGBTQ section, a Spanish-language section, Native American authors, regional history and Palm Springs architecture. The city's visitor listing gives 10 to 6 every day; another directory lists shorter weekday hours, so call (760) 933-3619 before you walk over.

culture.name: The Shops at Thirteen Forty-Five
culture.address: 1345 North Palm Canyon Drive, Palm Springs, CA 92262
culture.note: Zone 1, Uptown. The mid-century furniture and vintage stretch of N Palm Canyon runs north from Alejo Road, and this is the one-stop version of it: vintage and modern furniture, art, jewelry, resort wear, a bookstore and a café under one roof, by its own page. Open Thursday to Monday 10 to 6 (Oct 2026); (760) 464-0480. The other shops cluster in the 600 and 700 blocks (Modern Way 745, Bon Vivant 751, Iconic Atomic 724, per Visit Palm Springs, Dec 2025).

culture.name: Hunters
culture.address: 302 E Arenas Rd, Palm Springs, CA 92262
culture.note: Zone 1, Arenas Road, downtown: the dance bar, two rooms (bar and pool tables; dance floor), a patio, DJs, drag, karaoke, bingo, watch parties, by its own site. Founded 1998 by Mark Hunter Seymour; its own About page says "LGBTQ+ owned, inclusive and welcoming." Open every day 10 a.m. to 2 a.m. (Oct 2026); (760) 323-0700. Streetbar is across the street for the quieter drink.

culture.name: Streetbar
culture.note: Zone 1, Arenas Road, downtown, across from Hunters. Opened in 1991 as the first gay bar in Palm Springs, per Palm Springs Life: a neighborhood bar with a patio, locals through the day and visitors at night and on weekends. Open 10 a.m. to 2 a.m. every day, per the city's visitor listing. The plain answer to where to get a drink after the ride.

clubs.name: Desert Bicycle Club
clubs.note: The Coachella Valley's road club, based in Palm Desert. Guests are welcome and there's no sign-up, but you need to be comfortable in a group, and no aerobars. A groups (drop) and B groups (regroup) go out most mornings: {ride:palm-desert-ca-desert-bicycle-club-saturday-rides|the Saturday rides} from Palm Desert Civic Park, {ride:palm-desert-ca-desert-bicycle-club-sunday-climbers|Sunday Climbers} up Highway 74, {ride:palm-desert-ca-desert-bicycle-club-palm-springs-ride|a winter Monday ride to Palm Springs}, and weekday rides from Coffee Bean on El Paseo and from Bike N Brews that aren't in the directory yet; the club's calendar has them. From November the easier C rides (20 to 35 miles, about 13 to 14 mph) start from a different place each time and are posted on the club's C Rides Facebook page.

clubs.name: Tri-A-Bike
clubs.note: A Palm Desert bike shop at 44841 San Pablo Ave, (760) 340-2840. {ride:palm-desert-ca-tri-a-bike-saturday-fun-ride|Its weekly fun ride} leaves from the front of the store, and all types of bikes are welcome; the page says the rides start in October 2026. Distance and pace aren't posted, so call before your first one. The same page lists the shop's local routes and links a RideWithGPS account of Palm Springs-area rides.

clubs.name: Big Wheel Bikes CV
clubs.note: Shops in Palm Springs and Palm Desert. {ride:palm-springs-ca-big-wheel-bikes-community-group-rides|Its community group rides}, demo days, clinics and bike nights run in the November-to-April season and go up on its Instagram and Facebook, not on a fixed weekly slot, so follow the shop before you come. The Palm Springs store closes for the summer.

clubs.name: Great Outdoors (Palm Springs chapter)
clubs.note: An all-volunteer LGBTQIA+ and allies outdoor club with five Southern California chapters, Palm Springs among them; cycling and mountain biking are on its list. The latest Palm Springs bike outing a page showed was a Gay History Bike Ride in March 2025, about 18 miles from the Mizell Senior Center. Events are for members unless noted, so join before you plan on one.

bring_your_bike.summary: Bring it. Delta and American both check a packed bike as a standard bag, $45 each way (Oct 2026), so a round trip costs less than one day of a carbon rental. Alaska and Southwest did the same when their pages were last read (Sept 2026). If you would rather not fly with the case, Tri-A-Bike in Palm Desert receives a BikeFlights delivery, builds it for $150 and delivers to a Palm Springs hotel for $50 (Oct 2026). Rent only for a one-ride trip. Three valley shops rent carbon road bikes at $100 to $140 a day and deliver to Palm Springs; two of them set a two-day minimum on Tour de Palm Springs weekend. You do not need a car for the Tour or the valley floor. Highway 74, Joshua Tree and Box Canyon are car days.

airports.name: Palm Springs International
airports.note: In town: about two miles east of downtown, reached by Tahquitz Canyon Way from downtown or Kirk Douglas Way from the east (Wikipedia, Oct 2026). Alaska, Southwest, United, Delta, American, WestJet, Air Canada and Sun Country fly it, per a flight-search page dated Oct 2, 2026; Wikipedia adds Allegiant, Flair and Porter. Much of it is winter-only: Alaska's Boise, Everett and New York flights, Delta's Atlanta and Austin, United's Newark and Washington, Southwest's Austin and Chicago run roughly November to April or May (flight-search page, Oct 2026). Rental car counters are in the main building's north wing, and SunLine routes 2 and 4 run to downtown (Wikipedia). Taxi and rideshare pickup with a bike box: not confirmed; see the airport's ground-transportation page.

fly.airline_note: Delta, read on its own pages Oct 2026: a non-motorized touring or single-seat racing bike packed in a container built for bikes is checked baggage at the standard fee; 50 lb or more pays the overweight fee; over 115 linear inches or 100 lb is refused; a hard-shell bike case needs no release form, a soft bag signs a limited release; some Delta Connection flights exclude bikes. First bag $45, second $55 under 50 lb, US domestic Main Cabin. American, read Oct 3, 2026: one non-motorized bike in a hard case, a bike bag or a box built for bikes goes at the standard checked bag fee up to 50 lb; 51 to 70 lb pays the standard overweight fee; oversize fees do not apply; handlebars fixed sideways and pedals off or wrapped. First bag $50 at the airport or $45 online, second $60 or $55 online, updated May 18, 2026. Alaska and Southwest: read their pages before you book; on Sept 30, 2026 both checked a non-motorized bike in a case as a standard bag with oversize fees waived (Alaska also waives overweight to 70 lb), first bag $45, second $55. United, WestJet, Air Canada, Sun Country, Allegiant, Flair, Porter: not confirmed; read the airline's sports-equipment page. On every carrier confirmed here, a bike case under 50 lb is one ordinary checked bag.

ship.note: One valley shop says it on its own site: Tri-A-Bike in Palm Desert accepts shipped bikes, recommends bikeflights.com, and unboxes and assembles for $150; boxing it for the trip home is $100 to $150, and delivery to a Palm Springs hotel is $50 one way (Oct 2026). It is about 12 miles down the valley from downtown Palm Springs, closed Sunday and Monday, and asks for a call ahead. Both Trek stores and Bike N Brews box a bike to ship out ($79.99; $100 to $150, Oct 2026) but none says it receives one; Village Peddler lists "bike shipping" with no detail. Call before you ship anywhere but Tri-A-Bike. Carrier transit times, as read Sept 2026: BikeFlights by UPS with no stated day count and ShipBikes at no more than 6 business days one way in the continental US. Ship a week ahead and build in the shop's closed days.

shops.name: Tri-A-Bike
shops.note: Ship to the shop (it recommends bikeflights.com); unbox and assemble $150, box for the return $100 to $150, delivery to Palm Springs $50 one way (Oct 2026). Call (760) 340-2840 to book before you ship. Tuesday to Saturday 10 to 4, closed Sunday and Monday. 44841 San Pablo Ave, Palm Desert.

rent.note: Three shops, four stores, rent carbon road bikes: $100 to $140 a day, $300 to $400 a week (Oct 2026), one of them with Di2 (Tri-A-Bike). All four also rent full-suspension mountain bikes. Big Wheel on South Palm Canyon is the only fleet in Palm Springs; the rest sit in Palm Desert, about 12 miles down the valley, and deliver to Palm Springs for $50 (Big Wheel, Tri-A-Bike) or $100 (Bike N Brews). None lists frame sizes; call with your height. Big Wheel and Tri-A-Bike set a two-day minimum on Tour de Palm Springs weekend, so book early. No gravel rental was found; neither Trek store rents. The math: Delta or American checks your bike as a regular bag, $90 round trip paid online (Oct 2026), less than one day of a carbon rental, and shipping to Tri-A-Bike adds the carrier's charge plus $150 to build. Renting saves the case, the airport and the build; it costs more from the first day. For the Tour alone, renting is fair if you would rather not pack a bike for one ride. For a week, a fit you depend on, or a gravel bike, bring yours.

shops.name: Big Wheel Bikes CV, Palm Springs
shops.note: KHS Flite 720, carbon road: $105 a day, $250 for four days, $350 a week. KHS Flite Team road and KHS full-suspension mountain bikes: $80 a day, $195 for four days, $295 a week (Oct 2026). Helmet, lock and repair kit; $50 delivery; two-day minimum on Tour weekend. Sizes not listed for the road bikes. 1590 South Palm Canyon Drive; (760) 548-0500 ext. 1.

shops.name: Big Wheel Bikes CV, Palm Desert
shops.note: Ritte Esprit road bikes: SRAM Rival with aluminum wheels $105 a day, $250 for a half week, $350 a week; SRAM Force with deep carbon wheels $125, $295, $395 (Oct 2026). Clip-in or flat pedals; helmet, lock and repair kit; $50 delivery. Sizes not listed. 74200 Highway 111, Palm Desert; (760) 779-1837 ext. 2.

shops.name: Tri-A-Bike
shops.note: Cannondale or Giant road bikes: aluminum with 105 $75 a day, $200 a week; full carbon with Ultegra $100 a day, $300 a week; carbon with Di2 $124 a day, $350 a week. Full-suspension mountain bikes (Giant Stance 2 or Cannondale Habit) $80 a day, $250 a week (Oct 2026). Helmet, lock, seat-bag kit; $50 one-way delivery to Palm Springs; two-day minimum on Tour weekend. Sizes not listed. 44841 San Pablo Ave, Palm Desert; (760) 340-2840. Closed Sunday and Monday.

shops.name: Palm Desert Bike N Brews
shops.note: Road bikes: carbon $140 a day, $300 for three days, $400 a week; aluminum $100, $190, $300. Carbon full-suspension mountain bikes $125 a day (Oct 2026). No makes or sizes listed. Helmet and lock; reserve ahead; $100 pickup and drop-off in Palm Springs, up to five bikes. 73865 CA-111, Palm Desert; (760) 340-3861. Closed Sunday and Monday.

get_around.note: Not for a Tour weekend or a week of road riding on the valley floor. The airport is about two miles from downtown, the Tour starts downtown and packet pickup is downtown, Trek's repair shop and Big Wheel's rentals are on South Palm Canyon, and the Palm Desert shops deliver to Palm Springs hotels for $50 to $100 (Oct 2026). CV Link is three separate pieces, open 24 hours year-round with solar lights along parts of it (Coachella Valley Independent, April 2026): 19.6 miles from the Palm Springs Visitor Center at Highway 111 and Tramway Road along the Whitewater River to Date Palm Drive in Cathedral City; 5.4 miles in Palm Desert from the Bump and Grind trailhead to Cook Street; and 16 miles from Washington Street in La Quinta to Airport Boulevard in Coachella. Rancho Mirage and Indian Wells are not in the project, so the gaps between the pieces are on the road; the Arts and Music Line through La Quinta, Indio and Coachella starts construction in 2027 (CVAG, read Oct 2026). Highway 74, Joshua Tree and Box Canyon are car days; so is the Tram road if you would rather not ride the valley to it. The group rides start in Palm Desert, about 12 miles from downtown: ride there on CV Link and Highway 111, or drive. Driving in: downtown Los Angeles is about 100 miles west and downtown Phoenix about 260 miles east in a straight line; the road is longer. Out of PSP with a bike case: rental car counters are in the terminal's north wing (Wikipedia, Oct 2026); book an XL for a rideshare and expect the case to ride in the back. Tour de Palm Springs weekend, Feb 5 and 6, 2027: packet pickup Friday noon to 8 pm and Saturday from 6 am at South Palm Canyon and Baristo; the century rolls at 6:30 am from South Palm Canyon between Baristo and Tahquitz, the 16-mile route at 9:30; bike support at the start and at every SAG stop (the Tour's FAQ and registration page, Oct 2026).
get_around.transit_bike_rules: SunLine (the valley's bus), read Oct 2026: every SunBus has a front rack, no extra fare; a single-seat two-wheeled bike up to 69.5 inches long, 29-inch bars and 28-inch wheels fits; bikes do not ride inside unless they fold to the size of a suitcase; SunLine is not responsible for a bike on the rack. The page says nothing about e-bikes or weight. One way is $1, a day pass $3, exact cash or the Token Transit app (SunLine fares page, Oct 2026). Routes 2 and 4 link the airport and downtown (Wikipedia; SunLine's routes page lists the routes without endpoints). Fine for getting a built bike across the valley on a windy day; no use for a bike case.

bike_share.note: No bike share operates in the Coachella Valley that any page we read named (Oct 2026). Rent from a shop.

bring_your_bike.rules_and_safety: California, read Oct 2026. Drivers must give three feet when passing a bike (Vehicle Code 21760, the Three Feet for Safety Act); a driver in the same lane must change lanes to pass when one is open, and when three feet is not possible must slow to a reasonable speed and pass only when it does not endanger the rider. The fine is $35, $220 if a collision injures the rider (statute current through Sept 28, 2026). Helmets are required under 18 (21212). E-bikes come in three classes (312.5): class 1 pedal-assist to 20 mph, class 2 throttle to 20 mph, class 3 pedal-assist to 28 mph with a speedometer, rider 16 or older and helmeted; all under 750 watts. Ride as far right as practicable except when passing, turning left, avoiding a hazard or in a lane too narrow to share (21202). Sidewalk riding is set city by city (21206); check Palm Springs' own rule. California has no stop-as-yield law, but a rider may go on the walk signal, including a leading pedestrian interval (21456, per CalBike, page modified Aug 24, 2026). On CV Link, bikes share the path with e-bikes, scooters and low-speed electric vehicles, golf carts included; carts and low-speed vehicles are held to 20 mph, scooters and boards to 15 (CV Link FAQ, Oct 2026). On Tour day all kinds of bikes are allowed, recumbents, trikes and e-bikes included, and you need the helmet sticker to get into a SAG stop (the Tour's FAQ, Oct 2026). The read: Highway 111 is the valley's spine and its fast road. A cyclist was killed on it at Frank Sinatra Drive in Rancho Mirage on Jan 1, 2025 (KESQ, NBC Palm Springs), and another was critically hurt on it northwest of Gateway Drive in Palm Springs on March 4, 2026 (KESQ). The city's own March 2026 safety filing picks nine intersections to fix for night-time and bicyclist collisions, with lighting and leading pedestrian intervals: on Ramon Road, Sunrise Way, Gene Autry Trail, Indian Canyon at Vista Chino and three along Tahquitz Canyon Way (HSIP Cycle 11, CEQAnet, March 19, 2026). Those are the crossings between downtown and the airport. CV Link and South Palm Canyon are the quiet miles; the valley is open and windy, and the Independent's April 2026 guide tells path users to carry a neck gaiter for the wind and water for the heat. Highway 74 has little or no shoulder past the first few miles (PJAMM; the Desert Bicycle Club), and Tramway Road ends at a toll gate bikes can't pass.

travel_links.label: Tour de Palm Springs hotel list
travel_links.note: The Tour's own list of 21 Palm Springs hotels, grouped by distance from the start and finish: under 1, 2, 3 and 5 miles. The page says "Each hotel has special rates and incentives" and "For every booked room, the Tour de Palm Springs receives a donation towards our charities." Book with the hotel directly. Read Oct 4, 2026.

faq.q: Should I bring my bike to Palm Springs?
faq.a: Yes, for anything longer than the Tour itself. Delta and American check a packed bike as a standard bag, $45 each way (Oct 2026), and Tri-A-Bike in Palm Desert receives a shipped bike, builds it for $150 and delivers it to a Palm Springs hotel for $50. Renting is fair for a one-ride trip: Big Wheel Bikes on South Palm Canyon and two Palm Desert shops rent carbon road bikes at $100 to $140 a day and deliver (Oct 2026), with a two-day minimum on Tour weekend at two of them. No shop lists frame sizes, and no gravel rental was found.

faq.q: Do I need a car to ride in Palm Springs?
faq.a: Not for the Tour de Palm Springs or the valley floor. The airport is two miles from downtown, the Tour starts and packet pickup happens downtown, Trek's repair shop and Big Wheel's rentals are on South Palm Canyon, and CV Link runs 20 miles out of town without a car. The group rides start in Palm Desert, about 12 miles down the valley; ride there or drive. Highway 74, Joshua Tree and Box Canyon are car days.

faq.q: Where does the Tour de Palm Springs start?
faq.a: Downtown, on South Palm Canyon Drive between Baristo and Tahquitz. In 2027 the ride is Saturday, February 6: the century rolls at 6:30 a.m. and the 16-mile route at 9:30, and packet pickup is Friday noon to 8 p.m. and Saturday from 6 a.m. at South Palm Canyon and Baristo (the Tour's FAQ and registration page, Oct 2026). Koffi Palm Springs Central on Tahquitz Canyon Way opens at 6:30, and Sherman's Deli two blocks east opens at 8 for the plate afterward.

faq.q: Where do group rides start near Palm Springs?
faq.a: In Palm Desert, and guests are welcome with no sign-up. The Desert Bicycle Club's {ride:palm-desert-ca-desert-bicycle-club-saturday-rides|Saturday rides} leave Palm Desert Civic Park at 43900 San Pablo Ave in four groups; its {ride:palm-desert-ca-desert-bicycle-club-sunday-climbers|Sunday Climbers} leave the Starbucks at Highway 74 and El Paseo for the climb; in winter its {ride:palm-desert-ca-desert-bicycle-club-palm-springs-ride|Monday ride to Palm Springs} leaves Bike N Brews at 73865 Highway 111. {ride:palm-desert-ca-tri-a-bike-saturday-fun-ride|Tri-A-Bike's fun ride} leaves the shop at 44841 San Pablo Ave, any bike. In Palm Springs, {ride:palm-springs-ca-big-wheel-bikes-community-group-rides|Big Wheel Bikes' community rides} are posted on the shop's social accounts, November to April. The valley's rides hub is /rides/ca/palm-desert/.

faq.q: Is CV Link finished, and can I ride it end to end?
faq.a: It's finished as planned, but it isn't one path. CVAG opened about 40 miles in 2025 in three pieces: 20 miles from the Palm Springs Visitor Center to Date Palm Drive in Cathedral City, 5 miles in Palm Desert, and 16 miles from La Quinta to Coachella. Rancho Mirage and Indian Wells pulled out, so the gaps between the pieces are on the road. There are no posted hours, solar lights mark it at night, and you share it with e-bikes, scooters and golf carts held to 20 mph (CVAG, Oct 2026). Check CVAG's map for closures before a long ride.

faq.q: When is Palm Springs too hot to ride?
faq.a: Roughly May to October. PJAMM puts June-to-September highs at the foot of Highway 74 at 102 to 108 F and says not to start after sunrise then; Velo Palm Springs puts Joshua Tree's riding window at October to April and says the park's summer temperatures have reached 124 F; the Coachella Valley Independent (April 2026) tells CV Link users to ride early or late in summer. The season is October to April. The Tour de Palm Springs FAQ puts February highs at 60 to 70 and lows at 50 to 55.
